question: Why do some beings attain a level even higher than that enjoyed by Īśa?
premises: A trace of impurity causes a state of higher-and-lower differentiation.
The level enjoyed by Īśa is still marked by that differentiated condition.
Some beings can share in a level above that Īśa-enjoyed state.
inference: Because impurity still qualifies the Īśa-level, beings who transcend that qualification can attain a higher level.
uncertainties: The exact referent of ūrdhvapadabhāginaḥ (which class of beings) is not specified in this verse alone.
plain_english: Because a slight stain of impurity produces a state of higher and lower, even the level enjoyed by Īśa remains within that differentiation; therefore some beings can partake of a level higher than that.
